scope.order: numeric locus .1–.24, group index; six units frozen in first contract

fixed_contract_rules_verbatim:
R1. **Lexical lookup:** exact literal forms retrieve their fixed typed entries. Unassigned and variant strings remain explicit unknowns. No spelling normalization or automatic segmentation.

R2. **Prefix application:** an `APPLY_EVAL` head consumes exactly the immediately following three expressions of types ContextRef, KindRef, Outcome, in that order, producing one Atom. Atomic references/Outcome words require no reordering. Longer argument expressions would need an explicitly written new constructor, not a tacit lift. This law applies to every occurrence of the operation, not only .1.

R3. **Explicit binder opening:** a BIND_KIND head followed immediately by a KindDesc opens a Kind environment; a BIND_PAIR head followed immediately by a PairDesc opens a two-slot Context environment. An opener is consumed with its descriptor. Their remaining body is the complete following clause sequence within the current native scope unit. Heads do not themselves assert a body or fill an unknown clause.

R4. **Scope boundary license:** the six scope units are the first annulus .1, N .2–6, E .7–11, S .12–17, W .18–23, and final annulus .24. A lexical binder/modal opener scopes from just after its operand/head to the end of that unit, unless a later explicit closer is prospectively assigned and costed before full freeze. For this first contract **no closer is assigned**. A unit boundary closes all its scopes and clears references; line breaks inside a unit do not. This is one additional layout-based grammatical assumption, not an identified manuscript sentence boundary or speaker map. There is no implicit binder merely because a unit begins.

R5. **Nested scopes:** scope follows written opener order. A later binder of the same sort shadows the older binder only after its written occurrence; a reference always resolves to the nearest active matching binder. No backward binding. The first-annulus two applications therefore must remain under the same active Kind binder and same active pair binder; no intervening future lexical assignment may shadow either before G022 while still claiming this selected reuse.

R6. **Clause sequence:** adjacent complete Prop/Atom expressions form a conjunction in written order, within the same active scope. A bare descriptor, reference, operation value or unknown token is not a clause. No gap or unknown span is skipped to join two distant propositions. This rule creates no missing argument and contributes no covert IF/THEN.

R7. **Modal opening:** POSSIBLE opens modal scope over the conjunction of subsequent complete clauses within its scope boundary, with binders opened earlier outside that modal scope. It is one shared possibility claim, not proof of actual benefit/harm episodes. Modal distribution to separate worlds is not silently supplied. Joint possibility is an explicit exploratory strengthening/choice relative to merely stating two unconnected possibilities; if the source only licenses the weaker form, the departure remains recorded.

R8. **Binder closure:** at the declared scope end, form `exists k: D(k) and Body` or `exists c0,c1: PairDesc(c0,c1) and Body` in reverse nesting order. Descriptor conditions restrict the bound values; they do not produce observed individuals, material portions or events. Each open body must be fully parsed before a complete scoped proposition is claimed. Unknown body material makes the whole unit incomplete even where its local atoms can be exhibited.

R9. **No implicit assertion/coercion:** a well-typed local Atom is only asserted under the written enclosing scopes. A KindDesc is not a Kind, PairDesc not a Context, reference not its referent, and a modal proposition not actual truth. Additional higher-order constructors are not globally forbidden, but each must be a new explicitly written typed value/production, costed and shown in its actual occurrence. They cannot change R2's operator or reclassify a frozen entry to remove a local mismatch.

These nine rules are a concrete initial interface, not an unrestricted full grammar. Remaining syntax can be proposed during whole authorship only as new counted commitments preserving these definitions. The author cannot claim that unspecified prose syntax either automatically repairs every gap or proves global impossibility.

additional_rules.name: Finite typed prefix application
additional_rules.definition: A declared non-binder function consumes its required immediately following typed expressions in declared curried order. Functions explicitly required as arguments remain function values. This is typed application, not implicit conversion or reordering. APPLY_EVAL retains R2 exactly.

additional_rules.name: Explicit infix AND
additional_rules.definition: Prop ol Prop forms AND of the immediately adjacent complete propositions at the same active scope. It does not join incomplete spans, close scopes, or turn a noun/reference into a proposition.

additional_rules.name: Written modal closer
additional_rules.definition: shedaiin closes the nearest overt active modal head and returns POSSIBLE(conjunction of that completed body) as a Prop in the containing scope. It consumes no unknown body and does not close Kind/pair scopes. Unmatched use fails this production. This instantiates R4's prospectively allowed explicit closer, only after both selected health applications.

additional_rules.name: Descriptor-checked KindRef
additional_rules.definition: KindDesc D followed by KindRef r can form CheckedRef(D,r):KindRef only in an argument slot explicitly requiring KindRef. Resolution uses exactly resolve(r), with D(resolve(r)) as a side condition in the enclosing scope. It introduces no new kind and is not a KindDesc-to-Kind cast. Here THING is unrestricted and its test is trivially satisfied; that fact does not identify a concrete thing.

additional_rules.name: Explicit unit end
additional_rules.definition: END_UNIT is legal only as the last token of a fixed scope unit with every remaining body complete. It closes all remaining binders by R8, then the layout boundary has no remaining open scopes. No proposition is supplied by the marker; it cannot repair an incomplete body.

manual_units.translation: There is a generic thing and a choice of the two sick/healthy recipient contexts such that it is possible for those contexts to differ, the thing to require judgment, young and old to respond differently to cold/heat, and that same thing to benefit one recipient context and harm the other. Bodily natures vary over the year; the seasons differ in nature. Age and seasonal contrasts require judgment.
limits: Direction between sick/healthy and GOOD/HARM remains existentially unordered.
The first five propositions share possibility scope; later three assertions are outside it.
No patient, dose or actual treatment episode is named.

notes: sain, or, or, aiin, opchdy does not yet have a typed parse. aiin stays SEASONS. A proposed higher-order double-quantifier header was considered but not adopted; no values or rules for it exist in this packet.

manual_units.translation: There is a generic thing and a choice of two distinct temporal contexts such that it is possible for that thing to benefit in the first context, for the yearly cycle to vary, and for the same thing to harm in the second. Temporal contrasts require judgment; young and old differ in responses to cold/heat; seasons require judgment.
limits: All five propositions are inside one possibility scope.
The shared-temporal-input reading is the predeclared uncertain source interpretation.
The second evaluation incorporates a written context-reference instruction in tchedy; this is a charged lexical compound payload, not a discovered morphological decomposition.
k_T and k_H are different binders without an asserted equality.

manual_units.translation_initial_clause: Young and old differ in their responses across cold and heat.
notes: No modal/binder opener precedes this first S clause, so it is an unmodalized generic comparison. The rest of S is not parsed or asserted.
ar is PairDesc at every occurrence; no final annular ar/ar repair, aram split or reference cast is assigned.

manual_derivation_spans.derivation: BIND_KIND(THING): bind k_H; no assertion yet.
BIND_PAIR(HEALTH_PAIR): bind c_H0,c_H1; no assertion yet.
Open POSSIBLE; body begins at G006.
CLOSE_MODAL returns possibility of all five preceding body clauses; Kind/pair binders stay open.
Infix AND joins G024–26 with G028–31; no gap.
PAIR_REQUIRES_JUDGMENT(PAIR_UNION(AGE_PAIR,SEASON_PAIR)); layout then closes the two binders.
Infix AND; right operand starts G006 and continues through .9 G006.
CONJOIN_PREDICATION awaits YEAR, CYCLE_VARIES as a function value, and the complete second evaluation.
YEAR and CYCLE_VARIES are the first two written operands of CONJOIN_PREDICATION.
Close the single POSSIBLE scope after all five body clauses.
END_UNIT closes pair/Kind binders, only at the actual end of E.
DIFFERENTIAL_RESPONSE(AGE_PAIR,COLD,HEAT), with no preceding modal scope in S.

semantic_definitions.reference_policy: Exactly the frozen nearest overt matching binder; no cross-unit carry. All aliases are additional freely assigned whole values, never transcription normalization.
semantic_definitions.AGE_PAIR: P(c0,c1) iff {c0,c1}={AtTime(YOUNG),AtTime(OLD)} and c0!=c1. YOUNG/OLD are generic life-stage TimeSituation values, not individuals or ranked thermal properties.
semantic_definitions.SEASON_PAIR: P(c0,c1) iff c0=AtTime(s0), c1=AtTime(s1), s0,s1 in SEASONS, s0!=s1.
semantic_definitions.TIME_PAIR: P(c0,c1) iff c0=AtTime(t0),c1=AtTime(t1), t0!=t1; no event, patient or concrete date supplied.
semantic_definitions.DIFFERENTIAL_RESPONSE: For the supplied P,h0,h1: for each (c0,c1) satisfying P, ResponseProfile(c0,[h0,h1]) != ResponseProfile(c1,[h0,h1]). This is undirected profile inequality, not a GOOD/HARM inversion, individual episode, or equality of evaluated input across age/time/health passages.
semantic_definitions.DIFFER_IN: For the named comparison domain/aspect, members are generically nonuniform in that aspect. No assignment of each member to a named quality is supplied.
semantic_definitions.EVAL_AT_CONTEXT_1: lambda rK,o. ApplyEval(REF_CONTEXT_1,rK,o;env). Its additional lexical payload explicitly embeds a reference and partial application; no cut or phonetic compositional claim.
semantic_definitions.CONJOIN_PREDICATION: lambda y:TimeCycle, P:(TimeCycle->Atom), Q:Prop. AND(P(y),Q). One extra higher-order whole value with two operations; no hidden subject or predicate.
semantic_definitions.R13_side_condition: THING(resolve(REF_KIND)) is guaranteed by the same overt input binder; CheckedRef never chooses an input by description.
semantic_definitions.DISTINCT_CONTEXTS: lambda r0,r1. resolveContext(r0,env) != resolveContext(r1,env); undefined if either reference is unbound.
semantic_definitions.INPUT_REQUIRES_JUDGMENT: lambda rK. RequiresJudgment(resolveKind(rK,env)); undefined if unbound. The named faculty/requirement are openly charged lexical payload, not a patient or an implied treatment event.
semantic_definitions.normative_predicates: RequiresJudgment and the pair/domain versions are primitive normative relations on their declared written arguments. They do not imply actual successful conduct, a named physician, or a clinical prescription.

additional_type_definitions.TimeCycle: Generic cycle sort; YEAR is not a dated episode or a Context.
additional_type_definitions.ThermalCondition: Environmental-condition sort containing COLD and HEAT. Neither is an Outcome or a property of an assigned patient.
additional_type_definitions.SeasonDomain: Sort of generic seasonal domains; SEASONS is its sole assigned constant. No cardinality or figure mapping is encoded.
additional_type_definitions.ComparisonDomain: Written MEMBERS(SEASONS) returns the seasons as a domain of comparison. This explicit constructor is not a silent domain coercion.
additional_type_definitions.Aspect: Comparison respect; NATURE is the assigned value.
additional_type_definitions.NaturalAspect: A collective natural attribute, here BODILY_NATURES. It is not silently coerced to Aspect, Body, or a Kind.
additional_type_definitions.ModalCloser: Syntactic closer requiring an active modal head; it is neither an Atom nor an argument value.
additional_type_definitions.ScopeEnd: Syntactic end marker requiring completed bodies at the actual end of the current six-unit partition.
additional_type_definitions.LifeStage_TimeSituation: YOUNG and OLD are modeled as generic life-stage TimeSituations. This is a new ontology choice, not an identity of an age class with a physical individual. It uses the frozen AtTime constructor without adding a new Context tag.
